statement: Let H be the seven-vertex graph S_{2,1,1} disjoint-union K_2, with copies interpreted injectively and non-induced as in problem.md. For every integer m >= 3, the bipyramid B_m = overline(K_2) + C_m is a finite simple maximal planar graph, and the edge-colouring in which every apex--rim edge is red and every rim-cycle edge is blue contains neither a red nor a blue copy of H. Since |V(B_m)| = m+2, an avoiding maximal-planar graph exists at every order n >= 5. Consequently no eventual-unavoidability threshold N exists, and the frozen assertion in source.md is false.
contribution: A complete explicit disproof of the frozen disconnected diagonal maximal-planar Ramsey assertion by a uniform every-order counterexample family. The proof classifies all red fork embeddings and proves maximal planarity for every m >= 3, including the boundary m=3. This resolves only the stated specialization of the broader disconnected classification problem; the bounded literature comparison supports no priority or exhaustive novelty claim.
